scope.problem: vendor memory labels, shared-memory semantics, peak bandwidth, measured bandwidth, power, software maturity, and dated price observations are otherwise easy to conflate
scope.today: the repository has machine catalogs and a long-context estimator, but no compact dated purchase-class inventory joining those facts
scope.better_because: each decision datum is source-addressable and typed as measured, official_spec_derived, analytically_derived, or assumption_speculative
scope.witness: this JSON plus the rendered README and dated note
scope.not_a_claim: These are hardware inputs and evidence bounds, not measured fak-native Qwen3.8 or GLM-5.3 performance.

provenance_classes.measured: Direct observation or third-party measurement under a named configuration; measurement scope is preserved.
provenance_classes.official_spec_derived: Direct official vendor specification or arithmetic conversion of an official specification.
provenance_classes.analytically_derived: Transparent arithmetic or classification derived from cited inputs.
provenance_classes.assumption_speculative: Explicit planning assumption that must be replaced by a local observation before a performance claim.

unit_conventions.GB: decimal, 1000000000 bytes, used for bandwidth and vendor price-sheet labels unless a source explicitly says otherwise
unit_conventions.capacity_normalization: Vendor DRAM capacity labels are retained verbatim as marketed GB. estimator_physical_memory_bytes normalizes one labeled GB as one GiB-sized DRAM capacity because these products are assembled from binary-capacity DRAM devices; that normalization is analytically_derived, not a quoted vendor byte count.
unit_conventions.bandwidth: bytes per second; advertised values are ceilings, not sustainable inference rates
unit_conventions.price: nominal US dollars before tax, shipping, support upgrades, and missing components unless noted

estimator_mapping.bandwidth_bytes_per_second: No platform-wide range is manufactured. Use platform.bandwidth.sustainable_measured_bytes_per_second only when its measurement scope matches the workload; otherwise collect a workload-specific lower and upper bound.
estimator_mapping.compute_flops: The inventory records format capability and any cited peak, but does not fabricate a cross-format compute range. Match precision, sparsity, batch, and kernel support before supplying compute_flops.
estimator_mapping.efficiency_fraction: Not inventoried; it is workload/backend-specific and must remain an explicit estimator assumption or measurement.

limitations: Shared or unified system memory is not discrete VRAM. Capacity available to one inference process is lower than installed memory and depends on OS, driver, display, runtime, and allocator policy.
Advertised bandwidth is a physical or architectural peak. Host STREAM, GPU microbenchmarks, and inference effective bandwidth are different measurements.
A single measured maximum does not establish the lower/upper BandwidthBytesPerSec range required by the estimator.
TOPS/PFLOPS figures depend on precision, sparsity, accumulation, shape, and software support; they are not throughput predictions.
Prices are configuration- and date-specific and exclude tax. Framework and Dell configurations omit components explicitly noted in their price boundaries.
The Apple M5 Max row was a preorder on the as-of date, so sustainable measurements and street price are intentionally null.

No row is a measured fak-native Qwen3.8 or GLM-5.3 performance result. Final API-versus-local decisions require quality-qualified completed-job cost and completion time, including failed, retried, setup, queueing, and power costs.
